items.title: Inferno Drainer Is Burning Out
items.summary: Inferno Drainer and its many derivatives constitute arguably the most notorious cryptodrainer-as-a-service ecosystem ever developed. After months spent reverse-engineering its newest payloads and monitoring the ecosystem in real time, one thing seems clear: the operation is in serious decline, and has been for quite some time.

items.title: XCTDH Adopts Hash Hiding
items.summary: A blockchain-based C2 technique discovered in the XCTDH campaign's September 2026 evolution, where C2 addresses are steganographically encoded in Ethereum transaction destination addresses.

items.title: MacOS ClickFix AMOS Campaign
items.summary: A Fake “Bot Protection” Prompt Is Stealing Mac Users’ Crypto Wallets, and the Cleanup Is Not Keeping Up

items.title: CRPx0 ClickFix Ransomware Analysis
items.summary: CRPx0 is a ClickFix-delivered ransomware-as-a-service operation whose lures impersonate Windows and macOS update prompts and reCAPTCHA checks to trick victims into running a copied command. Ransom-ISAC traces the full killchain — from the ClickFix HTML through a multi-stage DLL loader to cross-platform Python ransomware that exfiltrates data before encrypting with AES-128 and RSA-4096 — with detections, YARA/Sigma logic, MITRE ATT&CK mapping and IOCs.

items.title: Infrastructure Destruction Squad / BLACKNET-00: Ransomware, Firebase and ICS Tooling
items.summary: A Billie Eilish superfan, two visible operators and three tested tools sit at the centre of this assessment. Ransom-ISAC analyses BLACKNET-00's ransomware builder, the Shadow Ghost Firebase scanner and the TRK-25 ICS reconnaissance toolkit — separating low-confidence marketing claims from verified, operationally relevant capability.

items.title: Weaponizing Exposed Data
items.summary: Ransomware and data-extortion groups are moving beyond bulk dumps to analyze, index and price stolen data before it is published or sold — removing the "weaponization tax" and turning breaches into searchable, tranched and targetable assets. Case studies on FulcrumSec, The Gentlemen, Titan, Sentap, ShinyHunters and the Leak Bazaar indexing-as-a-service platform, plus the emerging risk of soft-data pivots.

items.title: The Telegram Malware Ecosystem
items.summary: How a 9,898-row intelligence collection was built from Telegram bot tokens and chat IDs leaking out of malware on VirusTotal — covering 9,678 bot tokens, 9,756 sample hashes, and 6,512 destination chats, enriched via the Bot API and clustered into 854 operator campaigns, with attribution case studies including a crypto-drainer MaaS and an account-takedown service.

items.title: Cl0p Exploitation of PTC Windchill & FlexPLM (CVE-2026-12569)
items.summary: A coordinated Unified Threat Advisory covering active Cl0p ransomware affiliate exploitation of internet-exposed PTC Windchill and FlexPLM deployments — chaining a pre-auth FlexPLM WSDL information disclosure with a Windchill login servlet flaw for unauthenticated RCE, JSP webshell deployment, and double-extortion data theft.

items.title: The Fox Tempest Question
items.summary: One malware build split across two unrelated signing chains: a loader signed by a Chinese shell company via Certum, and a stealer signed under a stolen identity via Microsoft Trusted Signing — timestamped 11 days before Microsoft disclosed Fox Tempest, suggesting a Dragon Breath-aligned actor buying certificates from signing-as-a-service brokers.

items.title: MuddyWater: ClickFix to Telegram & PatchAgent Backdoor
items.summary: Full reverse engineering of a three-stage PatchAgent loader chain assessed as MuddyWater-linked with high confidence — from a regsvr32-executed COM dropper through an AES-256-CBC PTCH v2 container to a functional HTTP shellcode backdoor that hollows notepad.exe and beacons to operator infrastructure, all from ClickFix delivery containing Telegram beaconing.

items.title: Kali365 PhaaS Kit: OAuth Device-Code Phishing Enables MFA-Satisfied Token Theft
items.summary: End-to-end reverse engineering of the Kali365 (K365) Microsoft 365 Phishing-as-a-Service operator client, purchased web panel, and payment infrastructure — revealing OAuth device-code phishing (RFC 8628) that satisfies MFA legitimately to steal long-lived refresh tokens.

items.title: Kairos Ransomware: Data-Extortion Case Study Involving a U.S. Government Entity
items.summary: A leaked negotiation transcript and payment-flow analysis of a successful $1 million ransom payment by a U.S. government body to Kairos — a data-extortion actor whose "ransomware group" status remains unverified — including fund tracing to ByBit, OKX, and BELQI exchange touchpoints.

items.title: When Three Threats Meet One Inbox Against Japan
items.summary: Three unrelated Chinese-nexus operators — CoGUI email phishing, the Smishing Triad SMS/iMessage ecosystem, and MirrorFace espionage — converge on Japanese inboxes simultaneously, producing a single-campaign illusion that demands durable behavioral detection over short-lived IoCs.

items.title: ShinyHunters: Silent Malware as a Service (MaaS)
items.summary: A full malware analysis of Illusion-2.6.5-setup.exe — a deployment of Silent Stealer v2.6.5 and integrated RAT sold as a Malware-as-a-Service and distributed via Telegram under the ShinySpider alias, with an exposed operator panel that maps the complete C2 infrastructure and capability set.

items.title: The Gentlemen Leak Analysis (Part 2) — JA456 Follow-on
items.summary: Analysis of JA456, a follow-on package to the original Gentlemen Leaks that exposes operator-side artifacts — MEGA session history, a Synology NAS shadow dump, and wipe-in-progress screenshots — yielding rare attribution pivots including an early residential Izhevsk IP.
